chunks: Visiting Fatimah, daughter of the Prophet (peace be upon her and upon her father, husband, and sons). The compiler of this book—may Allah have mercy on him—stated: Narrations differ regarding the burial place of Fatimah, the Lady of the Women of the Worlds, peace be upon her. Some narrated that she was buried in al-Baqi', and some narrated that she was buried between the grave and the pulpit, and that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, said: 'What is between my grave and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise' because her grave is between the grave and the pulpit. And some narrated that she was buried in her house, so, and when the Banu Umayyah expanded the mosque, it became part of the mosque, and this is what I consider correct.

And indeed, when I performed Hajj to the Sacred House of Allah, my return was to Medina by the grace of Allah, the Exalted, whose name is glorified. When I finished visiting the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, I proceeded to the house of Fatimah, peace be upon her, which is from the column near which one enters through the Gate of Jibril, peace be upon him, to the rear of the enclosure in which the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, is. So I stood near the enclosure, to its left, and made my back face the Qiblah, and faced it with my face while I was in a state of ritual bath, and I said:

"Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Prophet of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Beloved of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Friend of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Chosen of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the Trustworthy of Allah. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the best of Allah's creation. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the most excellent of Allah's Prophets, Messengers, and Angels. Peace be upon you, O daughter of the best of creation. Peace be upon you, O Mistress of the women of the worlds, from the first to the last. Peace be upon you, O wife of the Guardian of Allah and the best of creation after the Messenger of Allah. Peace be upon you, O mother of Hasan and Husayn, the chiefs of the youth of Paradise. Peace be upon you, O truthful martyr. Peace be upon you, O content and satisfied one. Peace be upon you, O virtuous and pure one. Peace be upon you, O heavenly human. Peace be upon you, O pious and pure one. Peace be upon you, O inspired and knowledgeable one. Peace be upon you, O oppressed and usurped one. Peace be upon you, O persecuted and subdued one. Peace be upon you, O Fatimah, daughter of the Messenger of Allah, and the mercy and blessings of Allah be upon you."

May Allah bless you and your soul and your body. I testify that you departed upon clear proof from your Lord, and that whoever pleases you has pleased the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and whoever distances himself from you has distanced himself from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and whoever harms you has harmed the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and whoever connects with you has connected with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family, and whoever severs ties with you has severed ties with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him and his family. For you are a part of him, and his soul which is between his sides, as he, upon him be the best of Allah's blessings and peace, said.

"I call Allah, His messengers, and His angels as witness that I am pleased with whom you are pleased with, displeased with whom you are displeased with, disassociated from whom you have disassociated from, loyal to whom you have been loyal to, hostile to whom you have been hostile to, hating whom you have hated, loving whom you have loved, and sufficient is Allah as Witness, Reckoner, and Rewarder."

Then I said: 'O Allah, bless and send peace upon Your servant and Messenger Muhammad ibn Abdullah, the Seal of the Prophets and the best of all creation. And bless His Successor Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Commander of the Faithful, the Imam of the Muslims, and the best of the Successors. And bless Fatimah bint Muhammad, the Mistress of the Women of the Worlds. And bless the two chiefs of the youth of Paradise, Hasan and Husayn. And bless Zayn al-Abidin Ali ibn Husayn. And bless Muhammad ibn Ali, the Emitter of the Knowledge of the Prophets. And bless the Truthful from Allah, Ja'far ibn Muhammad. And bless the Containing Anger for Allah, Musa ibn Ja'far. And bless Al-Rida, Ali ibn Musa. And bless Al-Taqi, Muhammad ibn Ali. And bless Al-Naqi, Ali ibn Muhammad. And bless Al-Zaki, Hasan ibn Ali. And bless the Hujjah, the Qa'im, son of Hasan ibn Ali.'

'O Allah, give life to him with justice, and make him kill tyranny, and adorn the earth with the length of his stay, and manifest through him Your religion and the Sunnah of Your Prophet so that nothing of the truth is hidden out of fear of any of the creation. And make us among his helpers and followers and those accepted in the group of His allies, O Lord of the Worlds.'
'O Allah, bless Muhammad and his household, whom You have removed impurity from and purified with a thorough purification.'

key_terms.الْمِنْبَرُ: The pulpit in the Prophet's Mosque
key_terms.بَضْعَةٌ: A part of the body, indicating close kinship

ai.seo_question: What is the location of Fatimah's grave according to the compiler of Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih and what are the key elements of her Ziyarah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq presents the widely accepted Shia view that Fatimah (peace be upon her) is buried in her private quarters, which later became part of the Prophet's Mosque, contrasting it with other traditions placing her in Al-Baqi. The text serves as a liturgical model for pilgrims, emphasizing her status as 'Baz' (a part of the Prophet's body) and linking her personal virtues to the broader lineage of the Twelve Imams. This ziyarah underscores the theological concept of familial continuity in leadership and piety, reinforcing the authority of the Ahl al-Bayt.
